arguments.explanation: All four parts were placed. Re-checked at run end against each placement frame's LIVE (current) pose -- necessary because the frames move with the fixture and the fixture itself moved during the run -- all four parts are within their registry position and orientation tolerances: u_brown 1.7mm, u_orange 2.1mm, line_green 10.3mm (tol 15mm), inverted_u_yellow 2.9mm; all orientations well under their 10deg tolerances. However, several standing departures occurred during the run and are not erased by the acceptable final geometry: (1) an in-hand slip of u_orange during its place_approach step led to it contacting and disturbing the already-seated u_brown by ~22.8mm, exceeding u_brown's 10mm tolerance at that time; (2) an in-hand slip of line_green (0.0204m vs 0.02m tolerance) caused its place step to miss its placement frame by ~21.4mm/~25.5deg at that time (a place-step failure), and it was further disturbed by ~26.8mm during the subsequent place_inverted_u_yellow step; (3) base1, the fixture, which the specification requires stay undisturbed since it is never picked, shifted ~12.4mm from its initial rest pose over the course of the run, confirmed by a matching shift in all four of its attached placement frames -- this has no registry tolerance (base1 carries no spec block) but is a clear departure from the plain-language requirement and remains uncorrected at run end. All five bystander objects (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red, base2) were confirmed unmoved at run end, within floating-point noise of their initial poses, with no monitor fires against them. Grasp/clamp-effort monitors for all four parts never fired. Per standing instructions, none of these findings were acted on by retrying, reseating or aborting; the plan was carried through to completion. The run is judged non_conformant because the base1 fixture disturbance is a standing, uncorrected violation of an explicit instruction requirement, independent of the parts' final placement geometry being acceptable.
